title: Security Positioning & Claims Matrix for Enterprise Bids
content:
Purpose:
This brief is a lightweight, sales-friendly positioning and internal claim matrix we can use in RFP responses, executive briefings, and pre-sales technical reviews. It focuses on three priorities customers ask about: SOC2 readiness, ISO/HIPAA posture, and audit-log/data handling language for contracts. The goal: provide short, accurate sentences for sales + CSE to quote and a short ‘what we really mean’ internal note for legal/infra teams.

Audience and expected use:
- AEs and CSEs during discovery and security deep-dives.
- Solutions/SMEs prepping for SOC/ISO/HIPAA RFP sections.
- Contract countersigns and security Q&A decks (1-2 slide excerpt).

High-level positioning summary (customer-facing):
- "Redwood Inference is production-grade by design: we operate an audited control plane, provide tenant-isolated dedicated capacity, and offer private/VPC deployments for regulated workloads. We support SOC 2 type II certifications, ISO 27001-aligned controls, and HIPAA-compliant deployment patterns with BAAs for covered use cases."

Concise claim language (sales-usable, single sentences):
- SOC2: "Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II readiness; we regularly run control audits and provide SOC 2 reports under NDA or as part of Due Diligence for enterprise contracts."
- ISO: "Our information security program is aligned to ISO 27001 controls; we provide policy artifacts and evidence for ISMS activities on request during procurement."
- HIPAA: "We support HIPAA-compliant deployments (VPC/private deployment) and will sign BAAs for covered customers; PHI should be routed to dedicated/private deployments per our deployment guidance."
- Data handling: "We isolate customer data at rest with customer-configurable KMS keys and retention controls; default logs are retained for 90 days with extensions available under contract."
- Audit logs: "We provide immutable audit logs with event-level granularity (auth, model selection, request metadata, and admin actions). Audit logs can be exported to customer S3 or syslog destinations for retention and SIEM ingestion."

Internal explanatory notes (what these claims actually mean):
- "SOC 2 Type II readiness" = we currently have documented controls, regular internal audits, and a roadmap to a Type II attestation within the next 12 months; we can share SOC2 readiness artifacts but not a published Type II report unless attested. For RFPs asking for 'Type II report', route to Legal/Episodes.
- "ISO aligned" = policies and control families mirror ISO 27001; we currently map controls to ISO clauses in Confluence page SEC-ISO-MAPPING-2025. Full certification requires an external audit (customer should ask if certification is required).
- "HIPAA-compatible" = our product supports the technical and administrative safeguards commonly required (encrypt-at-rest, TLS-in-transit, access logs, role-based access). Customers wishing to process PHI must use Private or Dedicated deployments and enter a BAA.

Claims matrix (short form; use in RFP table):
- Control/Question: SOC 2 Type II report availability -> Customer-facing: "Available under NDA / enterprise pipeline" -> Internal note: "We can produce readiness artifacts; official report pending attestation Q3 2026."
- Control/Question: ISO 27001 certificate -> Customer-facing: "Aligned controls; documentation available" -> Internal note: "Mapping available; no certificate yet unless customer requires certified provider."
- Control/Question: HIPAA / BAA -> Customer-facing: "BAA available; recommend Private/Dedicated" -> Internal note: "Legal to draft BAA template; infra to verify deployment guardrails and logging for PHI."
- Control/Question: Audit log retention-> Customer-facing: "Default 90 days; configurable retention and export" -> Internal: "Can route logs to customer S3; retention config ticket INFRA-5782."
- Control/Question: KMS / key ownership -> Customer-facing: "Support for customer-managed KMS in Private deployments" -> Internal: "KMS integrations via AWS KMS / GCP CMEK; documented caveats in Confluence."

Competitive differentiation (how to frame vs major cloud-saas vendors):
- Focus on unified interface + deployment elasticity: "Unlike vendors who force you into their multitenant endpoint, Redwood gives the same API surface across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so teams can start quickly and then move to isolated capacity as risk or scale changes."
- Emphasize operational controls and exports: "We prioritize auditability: logs are first-class exports, not behind support tickets."
- Positioning versus full-managed cloud providers: "We provide inference-optimized runtime and deployment patterns that reduce per-token risk and make audit evidence straightforward — not a bespoke engineering project for each audit."

Example audit-log language for contracts and security questionnaires (short paragraphs):
- "Audit logging: Redwood generates immutable audit logs capturing all administrative actions, authentication events, model selection and versioning actions, request metadata (timestamp, route, latency buckets, anonymized token counts), and export actions. Customers can configure export to their cloud storage or SIEM for long-term retention. Logs are stored with integrity protections and tamper-evidence; access to log exports is controlled via RBAC and KMS-protected credentials."
- "Retention & deletion: By default, runtime telemetry and request metadata are retained for 90 days. Customers can opt-in for extended retention periods via contract. For Private deployments, data retention and deletion policies are implemented using customer-specified retention windows and KMS lifecycle policies."

Short FAQs for sales + CSE to memorize:
- "Do you sign BAAs?" -> "Yes, for customers processing PHI on Private/Dedicated deployments. Work with Legal to scope."
- "Can we get SOC 2 report now?" -> "We provide readiness artifacts and control mapping; SOC 2 Type II report will be available to enterprises under NDA after attestation. See Legal."
- "Can logs be exported to our SIEM?" -> "Yes, S3/Syslog/Splunk exports supported for Hosted+Dedicated; Private deployments can keep logs on customer infrastructure."

Open questions / action items (for internal follow-up):
- Legal: finalize BAA template and approval flow (owner: Maya Chen) — jira:LEGAL-2031
- Infra: validate KMS integration edge cases for cross-region private deployments (owner: Diego Alvarez) — jira:INFRA-5782
- Compliance: confirm timeline for SOC 2 Type II external attestation and prepare PR for readiness artifacts (owner: Ethan Roarke)
- GTM: produce 1-slide security sell-sheet and a short email template for AEs to attach in initial outreach (owner: Aisha Patel)

Examples / snippets (one-liners for slide decks):
- "Enterprise-ready controls, flexible deployment modes: Hosted API, Reserved/Dedicated pools, and Private/VPC."
- "Audit logs exported to your storage; retention & KMS ownership configurable by contract."

Related references (internal):
- Confluence: SEC-PLATFORM-COMPLIANCE-2025 (control docs)
- Infra ticket: INFRA-5782 (log export & retention enhancements)
- Legal draft: github:pr/rlw/baa-draft-v2
- Slack thread: #sec-sales-questions (pointer for real-time escalations)

Version notes and usage guidance:
- This doc is intentionally concise — feed these lines into RFP responses or the one-pager. Any deviation from the claim language above must be cleared with Legal/Compliance.
- Keep this doc in sync with the master compliance map in Confluence; if you spot mismatches in customer Q&A, add a comment and ping Compliance.
